Cross-ref: https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/andy-burnham-cabinet-bus-fares-b3019216.html ; https://www.gov.uk/government/news/cheaper-travel-for-millions-with-a-third-off-fares
NOTE (Wed 22 Jul) — Reaction to the £2 bus-fare cap / cost-of-living blitz:
- Shadow Chancellor Sir Mel Stride: govt is "not actually specifying where the money is going to come from"; "a worrying sign, we need to have a government which is on top of the public finances, not one that is making lots of spending commitments without explaining where the money is going to come from" (BBC Breakfast). Adds it "leads to a conclusion that we are probably heading towards tax increases."
- Tory leader Kemi Badenoch: "Where's the money coming from? I am very concerned the Prime Minister is making a lot of promises without giving the country an explanation about how we can afford them." (Also slammed Cabinet over prisoner-release joke — "disgusting".)
- Shadow transport secretary Richard Holden: "Labour increased this by 50% to £3 and now expect praise for returning it back down to £2 in line with the Conservative manifesto. The real question is how Labour will pay for these policies... borrowing or taxes will have to rise."
- Reform UK chairman Lee Anderson: any cost-of-living help welcome but Burnham "walked into No 10 with absolutely no plan".
- Lib Dem transport spokesman Olly Glover: "a relief to see the cap back down to £2" but "an easy win"; wants £1 national cap, 10% off rail, 10p/litre off fuel duty.
- Greens: lower fares no use if "buses aren't there"; want permanent free travel for under-22s.
- Bus/coach trade body CPT chief exec Graham Vidler: "pleased" buses are "at the heart of" govt's cost-of-living plans but calls it the "sixth continuation or extension" of the scheme since Jan 2023 and demands a "fair" reimbursement model to put operators on a "sustainable footing." Will work with govt "to make the £2 fare cap a success."
Transport Sec Heidi Alexander: "100% sure" money is there; "£454m of re-prioritising money... switch spending... those grants for international climate projects... we're going to be making those loans instead so that money comes back." Cap runs 1 Jan 2027 to end-2027 (England outside London; London already £1.75).
